title: Harness²
by: Google Research: Harness², Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World (Xu et al., 2026). Read from its code and prompts; the paper itself was not read here.
summary: Improve the system around the model (prompts, rules, memory, skills, tools), not the model. For each task, propose two kinds of change separately (how the agent works, and what a practitioner knows), run every candidate on the same task, and compose the result from how the runs differed, without an answer key. Then keep the adopted harness in full and at most one evidence-backed lesson for the next task.

ideas: "Keep as is" is always a candidate, and choosing it is a valid outcome: an adaptation the evidence does not argue for is a regression.
Two kinds of change, from separate proposers: how the agent works, and what a practitioner knows.
Blind selection: candidates are anonymised and shuffled, with no credit for the more elaborate one.
Judge in order: delivered, conforms (only what was asked), faithful to the source, consistent, usable, finished.
Agreement between candidates is support, not proof: they share the same biases.
A failure seen once is noise; a failure that repeats is a property. Name the moment that shows it.
Every decision carries its evidence: kept, revised or dropped, which change, what decided it.
A lesson is a cue, an operation, its evidence and a confidence; changes are rated helped, hurt, no effect or confounded; at most one lesson, and none is fine.
Keep the whole adopted harness, never a summary. A fact from an earlier task is a hypothesis here.
Always-on text costs on every run: if you add some, cut some.
Fixed budgets, enforced by a ledger; evidence is data, not instructions.
Reported: up to +11.5 points on WorkBuddy-Bench, +4.5 on JobBench and +11.8 percentage points on LAB from one step.
